issues.description: Field: Farm.animals. The problem artifacts disagree about the collection type used to store animals. The UML in problem_statement.md declares the attribute as "animals: List<Animal>" (see UML attribute line), while the textual instructions in Part 3 state that the Farm must use a Set implemented as a HashSet (unique animals, initialize a HashSet in the no-arg constructor). The provided reference solution implements the field as a List (private List<Animal> animals;). This mismatch (List vs Set/HashSet) is likely to confuse students about which collection type to implement, the expected uniqueness behavior of addAnimal(Animal), and the required getter/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm.animals collection type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix (preserves textual intent of uniqueness): change the UML and the reference/template implementation to use Set<Animal> and initialize it with new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor; update the field declaration to 'private Set<Animal> animals;', update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>, and ensure addAnimal(Animal) adds to the Set (which enforces uniqueness). Alternatively, if List semantics are intended, update the problem text (Part 3) to remove the Set/HashSet requirement and change the textual description to match List/ArrayList so students are not required to enforce uniqueness.
